title: Build a read-only Solana balance tool
goal: Create a small balance reader with an explicit network, public account and commitment level.
intro: An agent tool should expose a narrow operation and validate its arguments before making a request. This function reads a public account through Solana’s getBalance method and returns the integer amount in lamports with the RPC context. It can be connected to a tool-calling application after its inputs and errors have been tested.
requirements: Python 3.10 or later; this example uses only its standard library.
A base58 public account address that decodes to 32 bytes.
Access to the selected Solana RPC endpoint. Public endpoints have rate limits.
limits: This recipe does not sign or submit transactions and does not need a private key.
Devnet and Mainnet beta are separate networks. A balance on one is not a balance on the other.
Keep lamports as an integer. The preview validates the address shape and length, not the account’s purpose or existence.
steps: Start on Devnet and choose the commitment required by your application.
Change the account field and inspect the generated request and validation function.
Run the file and keep the network, commitment, lamports and context together.
Before attaching the function to an agent, define the allowed arguments and handle RPC errors, timeouts and rate limits in the host application.
checks: Only getBalance is requested; no transaction or signing method is present.
Invalid addresses and unsupported networks are rejected before a network request.
Large lamport values remain integers, and a JSON-RPC error stops processing.
tested_scope: Code syntax, address validation, network selection and mocked RPC responses checked locally. No agent integration or live RPC execution is claimed.
